paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The variation curve of k^⊤β for AlphaEdit and MEMIT as the number of edits increases, with GPT2-XL serving as the edited model. As the results of Llama3-8B are not suitable for display in a line chart, they are presented in Appendix <ref>.

model_annotations.English: The plot titled “GPT2-XL” illustrates how the metric \(k^\top \beta\) changes for two methods (AlphaEdit and MEMIT) as the number of edits increases. The x-axis represents the number of edits on a linear scale, spanning approximately 200 to 3000, with labeled ticks at 500-unit intervals (500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000). The y-axis is labeled \(k^\top \beta\) on a linear scale, with labeled ticks from about 0.002 to 0.012 in increments of 0.002 (0.002, 0.004, 0.006, 0.008, 0.010, 0.012), and the plotted values extending slightly above 0.012 near the maximum. The AlphaEdit series is shown as a red solid line with circular markers, decreasing across the x-axis from about 0.0040 at ~200 edits to about 0.0025 at 500, ~0.0018 at 1000, ~0.0015 at 1500, ~0.0013 at 2000, ~0.00115 at 2500, and ~0.00105 at 3000. The MEMIT series is shown as a light-blue solid line with circular markers, increasing across the x-axis from about 0.0045 at ~200 edits to ~0.0052 at 500, ~0.0066 at 1000, ~0.0081 at 1500, ~0.0094 at 2000, ~0.0106 at 2500, and ~0.0128 at 3000.
model_annotations.German: The plot titled “GPT2-XL” illustrates how the quantity \(k^\top \beta\) varies with the number of edits for two methods, AlphaEdit and MEMIT. The x-axis represents the number of edits on a linear scale, spanning from about 200 to 3000, with numeric tick labels shown at regular 500-step intervals (500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000). The y-axis is labeled \(k^\top \beta\) on a linear scale, ranging from 0 up to slightly above 0.012, with labeled ticks at approximately 0.002 intervals (0.002, 0.004, 0.006, 0.008, 0.010, 0.012). The AlphaEdit series is drawn as a solid red line with circular markers and decreases across the x-range, starting near 0.004 at ~200 edits and reaching about 0.0011 by 3000 edits, passing through intermediate points around 0.0025 (500), 0.0019 (1000), 0.0015 (1500), 0.0013 (2000), and 0.0012 (2500). The MEMIT series is drawn as a solid light-blue line with circular markers and increases across the x-range, starting near 0.0046 at ~200 edits and rising to about 0.0128 by 3000 edits, with intermediate values around 0.0052 (500), 0.0067 (1000), 0.0081 (1500), 0.0094 (2000), and 0.0106 (2500).
